output.brief:
The most likely cause is contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique, the new pads, or the new reporting app. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans during the bay closure, mostly from an old bulk drum that was left uncapped for a time. All 11 vans with complaints were serviced there. Two of them, tested on 24 Sep, had fluid boiling at about 150°C against 255°C for sealed stock. Water-laden fluid can boil in hot brakes on long descents, which matches the symptom "fine at the top, soft by the bottom". The same 19 drivers reported nothing in other vans, including on Upper Wend. Calder Road Garage vans, which had the same pads, had no complaints. Northfield warned Eastgate's workshop on 25 Sep and got no reply.

What to do this week: pull every Northfield-serviced van (13, including LK-214 and LK-227) from service, test the fluid, and renew it from sealed stock. Do not issue warnings or retrain drivers. That would punish people for reporting a real fault and discourage further reports. Hold off on changing pad supplier until there is evidence that pads are at fault. Confidence is high, but only two vans have actually been tested, so test them all.
